visual.general_description: Three side-by-side axial brain MRI slices at the posterior fossa level, each with a yellow arrow aimed at the brainstem.
visual.detailed_description: Three grayscale axial head MRI slices through the cerebellum, brainstem and skull base are placed side by side on black backgrounds, labelled a, b and c with white lowercase letters at upper left. Each slice carries one yellow arrow pointing from the upper left toward the brainstem just in front of the cerebellum, at the image-left side of midline. Panel a is dark with bright cerebellar hemispheres, scattered bright nasal/sinus signal and a small focal bright spot at the arrow tip. Panel b shows more anatomic detail with bright nasal cavity and sinus signal, gray cerebellum with folia and an arrow ending at the brainstem. Panel c shows bright fluid around the brainstem and between cerebellar folia with gray brain tissue and the arrow ending at the brainstem border. No text other than the panel letters is visible.
limitations: Image shows axial parenchymal sequences; the vertebral artery dissection and luminal reduction described in the caption are not visibly demonstrated in these three slices.
Low-resolution JPEG with no left/right marker, scale bar, window setting or slice-position text; laterality and lesion extent cannot be read from the image alone and are taken from the article text.
